ingredients.title: Chicken
items: 2 large chicken breasts, preferably bone-in and skin-on
1½ tsp kosher salt, plus more as needed
1 tbsp of high smoke point cooking oil

steps: Heat the oven to 450°F / 230°C.
Place the potatoes in a pot of generously salted water. Bring to a simmer and cook until just tender, about 8–12 minutes, depending on size.
Drain well and let them steam-dry for several minutes.
Gently crush each potato with the bottom of a glass or measuring cup. You want them flattened but still in one piece.
Transfer to a roasting tray. Toss generously with oil, thyme, garlic and salt.
Roast for 30–40 minutes, turning once, until deeply golden and crisp.
While the potatoes roast, place a large pan over medium heat.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Add the oil and place the chicken skin-side down. Don’t move the chicken around.
Cook for approximately 8–12 minutes, until the skin is deeply golden and crisp.
Turn the chicken over.
Add the butter, crushed garlic and thyme. Baste the chicken with the butter for 1–2 minutes.
Transfer the skillet to a 375°F / 190°C oven.
Cook until the thickest part of the breast reaches approximately 165°F / 74°C.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and let it rest for 5–8 minutes.
Leave the browned bits and chicken juices in the skillet.
Return the skillet to medium heat.
Add the minced shallot and garlic. Cook for about 1 minute, stirring frequently.
Add the sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for another 30 seconds.
Pour in the white wine and scrape the bottom of the skillet thoroughly to release all the browned chicken fond.
Increase the heat and reduce the wine until only a few tablespoons remain.
Add the chicken stock and reduce by roughly half.
Add the heavy cream and Dijon mustard.
Lower the heat and simmer gently for 2–4 minutes, until the sauce lightly coats the back of a spoon.
Remove the skillet from the heat.
Whisk in the Parmesan and cold butter.
Add the chopped tarragon, torn basil, lemon juice and plenty of freshly ground black pepper.
Taste and adjust the seasoning.
